title: Price-Match Terms of the Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
The price-match terms carried by each of the Air Ticket Fare Brands consist of a window, a permission and a ceiling.

**Price-match window.** The hours after ticket issue within which a lower public price may be claimed.

**Cash settlement permitted.** Whether a price-drop claim is settled in cash rather than refused.

**Settlement ceiling.** The ceiling on a single price-drop settlement per booking.

| Fare brand | Price-match window (hours) | Cash settlement permitted | Settlement ceiling (USD) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic Economy Lite | 0 | no | 0.00 |
| Economy Saver | 24 | no | 0.00 |
| Economy Classic | 24 | yes | 150.00 |
| Economy Flex | 48 | yes | 250.00 |
| Premium Economy Select | 48 | yes | 300.00 |
| Business Saver | 72 | yes | 400.00 |
| Business Flex | 72 | yes | 600.00 |

## Where the columns diverge

A window and a permission are scheduled separately, and Economy Saver shows why that matters: it carries a window of 24 hours yet is scheduled as not permitting a cash settlement, and its ceiling stands at 0.00 USD. Basic Economy Lite carries neither, its window being 0 hours.

Among the five brands scheduled as permitting a cash settlement, the ceiling rises with the brand, from 150.00 USD on Economy Classic to 600.00 USD on Business Flex, and the window lengthens from 24 hours through 48 to 72.

## Hypothetical settlement

A hypothetical Economy Flex booking meets a publicly offered price 310.00 USD lower within the scheduled 48 hours. The ceiling scheduled for that brand is 250.00 USD, so the settlement stands at 250.00 USD rather than at the whole difference. On a hypothetical Business Flex booking the same 310.00 USD difference falls below the scheduled ceiling of 600.00 USD and is not cut down by it.
